title: The outcomes log is scanned on every pass
evidence: True: due.rs:315-321 `rest_ends` loads every outcome of every source each pass; cache.rs:585-587 no LIMIT; `failures_in_a_row` (cache.rs:656-669) materialises the per-source log, called from due.rs:187, read.rs:70/84, figures.rs:400. But the log is capped at OUTCOMES_KEPT=1000 rows per source (cache.rs:41, pruned in `record` at cache.rs:573-577), so the scan is bounded and does not grow with the log or the book.
condition_or_scenario: A bounded scan (<=1000 rows per source) per pass; no scale at which it becomes a user-visible slowdown.

title: The chart read-ahead fetches every trade's chart, and each one is served as if the person opened it
evidence: App.svelte:224-236 reads every trade then calls `readAhead` for every trade and holding; ahead.ts:46-53 reads each chart not kept, one after another, 1-3 `/api/history` reads per trade (ahead.ts:19-35, chart.ts:96); a null (pending, no bars) result is not remembered. The `ahead` flag stays in the page (reads.svelte.ts:115-116), and feeds.rs:3248-3271 starts a background source read for any span whose bars are not stored or are stale (history.rs:508-522, :592-614). The owner's book has 646 trades (docs/plans/stage-p-capacity-and-process.md:45).

Ordinary: Clear data and a new browser are normal actions; 646 trades is this book.

title: Views are rebuilt whole and serialised to tell whether they changed
evidence: Code facts true: views.rs:197-199 `version_of` serialises; views.rs:271-282, :324-335, :771-773, :830-841 rebuild and diff whole; events.rs:512-515. Measured: feed-step at four times the owner's size 48 ms on a Mac, 101 ms Pi-scaled against a 95 ms budget, allocations 148K -> 712K from x1 to x4 (docs/plans/stage-3-the-brokers-statements.md:167); listed in capacity.rs:201-202 OVER_BUDGET. The budget is a share of the 60-second quote pass, not a person waiting.
condition_or_scenario: The measured miss is at four times the owner's size; at the owner's size the step is about a quarter of that (allocations 148K at x1). Needs a book ~4x larger to exceed even the background budget.
user_impact: None at this book's size; at ~4x the book a stream step for one signal takes ~0.1 s on a Pi.

title: A reconnecting page replays its first subscriptions, and stream ids restart at 1
evidence: live.svelte.ts:398-400 builds the EventSource URL once from `connectedWith` and the `have` of that moment; the browser's automatic reconnect reopens that URL; stream.rs:39-108 registers the URL's docs and sends their first messages at once (first=true, no wait); live.svelte.ts:430-446 applies a `snapshot` to whatever holder is wanted under that key, regardless of its params, and `keep(doc)` saves it under the current params (:506-520); only after `hello` does `sayWanted` post the current set (:408-429, :298-315). onerror (:484-488) only sets 'Could not reach Bagholder.'. The id restart is handled (:166 `if (n === 1) last = 0`).
condition_or_scenario: 1) Page open; the person changes a filter or sort on Trades, or scrolls so `limit` grows (subs.svelte.ts:101-103). 2) The stream drops: the server is restarted without a version change, the laptop sleeps and wakes, or the tunnel blips. 3) EventSource reconnects with the first-connect docs/have; the server snapshots Trades under the original params. 4) The page reconciles that into the current Trades holder and keeps it under the current params, until its own POST /api/events/watch lands and the right snapshot follows. Ordinary: restarts, sleep/wake and network drops.
user_impact: After a reconnect, a list whose filter, sort or length changed since the page loaded briefly shows the first-load version (rows vanish then return), and that copy is kept in the browser until the correction arrives.

title: Stream failures are swallowed
evidence: Code facts true: events.rs:442 catch_unwind then `continue`; events.rs:353 bad filters -> none (badge count only); docs.rs:164-167 `.ok()?`; stream.rs:119-124 `.ok()?`; live.svelte.ts:46-58 skips a patch to an unknown path. Each needs an internal failure: a panic in a document read, a SQLite error reading notifications, a page-built filter the server cannot parse, or a diff path the page lacks. The figure views already have a `refused` path. No commit, doc or issue records any of these occurring; the one real failure on record (8a11daed, a figures build refused at start) went through the header, not this path.
condition_or_scenario: Needs a document read to panic or the store to error, or a page/server mismatch in filters or patch paths; no evidence any has occurred.
user_impact: If it happened, a screen such as notifications would silently stop updating with no error in the header.

title: The browser's kept store has no bound and keeps whole documents
evidence: main.ts:17-20 mounts the page only after `keptIn` (live.svelte.ts:199) = kept.ts:79-107 has read every entry for the book into memory. Every non-ephemeral read answer is saved whole (reads.svelte.ts:121-125) and every drawn chart again (`remember`, reads.svelte.ts:165-168), so the read-ahead (#425) leaves ~2 entries per trade/holding chart; documents are saved per (key, params) (kept.ts:135-153, live.svelte.ts:506-520). Nothing evicts: `bookIs` (kept.ts:160-178) drops only other books' keys, and returns early when the book is the same. The owner's book has 646 trades.
condition_or_scenario: 1) Ordinary use: the read-ahead keeps each trade's and holding's chart twice; each new filter/sort combination adds a document copy. 2) Every later page open (main.ts:17) waits for kept.ts:89-101 to cursor through all of them before the first frame. Growth is per trade and per parameter set, never trimmed.
user_impact: Each page open waits for the browser to read every kept chart and screen before drawing; the wait and the storage grow with the trades and filter combinations used (size not measured).

title: The ETag is computed from the finished body, and each answer is kept twice in the page
evidence: True: http/mod.rs:263-282 runs the route, hashes the body, then answers 304; reads.svelte.ts:124-125 keeps a memory and an IndexedDB copy. A 304 costs the server what a 200 costs minus the transfer; on loopback or a tunnel the person sees the same answer time. No measurement shows either costing the person time.
condition_or_scenario: Constant overhead per conditional request and a second in-page copy; not growth the person meets as a slowdown (the stored-copy growth is #429).
user_impact: none

title: On-demand reads are not refreshed when the stream says their data moved
evidence: reads.svelte.ts:108 returns this page load's memory answer with no age unless `maxAgeMs` is given; chart.ts:96-97 `loadHistory` gives none and keys by `t.id|tf` (opts.key overrides the query, so the `to` date in chartSpan, chart.ts:66-71, is not in the key); the read-ahead (ahead.ts:46-53) fills that memory for every trade and holding at page load; memory is cleared only on a server restart (`askAgain`, chart.ts:76-77 via state.svelte.ts:65-70). TradeDetail.svelte:69-70 calls loadHistory, which answers from memory.
condition_or_scenario: 1) The person opens the app in the morning; the read-ahead reads every holding's chart into memory. 2) The page stays open (the app is meant to stay open with live quotes). 3) Hours or days later they open a holding or open trade. 4) TradeDetail.svelte:70 -> reads.svelte.ts:108 answers from memory without asking; the server is not asked again until it restarts or the page reloads.
user_impact: A holding's or open trade's chart opened in a page left open shows the bars as of page load, missing everything since, until the page is reloaded or the server restarts.

title: The number of rows shown is part of a subscription, so scrolling starts a new one
evidence: views.rs:72-73 `limit` is a subscription param; views.rs:175-176 builds Trades/Cashflow with it; events.rs:194 and :408 drop a view whose params changed; subs.svelte.ts:71-77 opens a new subscription per params; subs.svelte.ts:92-103 FIRST_ROWS=100, `more` adds 100. The new subscription is snapshotted whole (events.rs:512-515). The owner's book has 646 trades and 3,296 cash-only transactions (docs/plans/stage-3-the-record-by-change.md:61).
condition_or_scenario: 1) The person scrolls the Trades list (646 rows) or Cashflow (thousands of rows) to the end of what is shown. 2) subs.svelte.ts:101-103 raises `limit` by 100. 3) The page subscribes again; events.rs:408 drops the built view; the server rebuilds it and resends every row up to the new limit. Reaching row N of Cashflow resends ~N^2/200 rows in total. Ordinary: scrolling a long list.
user_impact: Each 'next 100 rows' waits for the server to rebuild and resend every row already shown; deep in Cashflow each step resends thousands of rows.

title: Unused routes and stream messages are still served
evidence: True: http/mod.rs:238 `/api/notifications/stream`, stream.rs:203-211; status.rs:70/:512 `StatusAnswer` at `/api/status`; the page uses neither (web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts:12-13 asserts it never asks). Nothing opens them, so the thread per open never runs in use.
condition_or_scenario: Dead code; nothing the person does reaches it.
user_impact: none

title: A hidden tab counts as watching
evidence: live.svelte.ts:288-297 `shownNow` sends every wanted doc with no `document.hidden` check (no visibility handling on subscriptions; only clock.svelte.ts and ShortInterest.svelte look at visibility); events.rs:225-227 `showing` is true while any stream holds a PRICED key; due.rs:158-160 then quotes every held listing, and due.rs re-arms every QUOTES_EVERY=60 s (due.rs:37).
condition_or_scenario: 1) The person leaves Bagholder on Portfolio or Markets in a background tab or minimised window (or leaves it open on another device). 2) The tab's EventSource stays open, its watch stands. 3) Every 60 s due.rs:128-129 quotes every held listing from the sources. Ordinary: a tab left in the background.
user_impact: While no one looks, every holding is still quoted every minute; nothing on screen is wrong, only requests made for nobody.

title: Each tab holds its own stream over HTTP/1.1
evidence: True: live.svelte.ts:400 one EventSource per tab, no SharedWorker/BroadcastChannel; server/Cargo.toml:50 axum `http1` only. Browsers allow six HTTP/1.1 connections per host. No doc, test or commit records the owner running six or more Bagholder tabs; a tunnel that speaks HTTP/2 to the browser would not hit the limit.
condition_or_scenario: Needs six or more Bagholder tabs open at once in one browser on a plain HTTP/1.1 connection; no evidence it occurs.
user_impact: A seventh tab's reads would wait for a connection that never frees, so it would hang loading.

title: Nothing the server sends is compressed, and the chart library sits in the main bundle
evidence: True: server/Cargo.toml:52 no compression feature; http/mod.rs:247-251 no compression layer; fillsChart.ts:1 and tradeChart.ts:1-11 import lightweight-charts statically; vite.config.ts has no chunking. On loopback it costs nothing. The repo has no measurement of transfer size or load time over the owner's tunnel, and does not say which tunnel it is or whether it compresses.
condition_or_scenario: Matters only on a link slow enough that uncompressed JSON and a larger first bundle are noticed; not measured or reported. Missing: the tunnel type and the transfer sizes.
user_impact: A first load or read-ahead over a slow link would move more bytes than needed; on the desktop, nothing.

title: The page announces what it wants once per document on first open
evidence: True: live.svelte.ts:218-225 `primed` deletes one doc and calls `sayWanted` per arriving document, so a first open posts /api/events/watch once per primed screen (live.svelte.ts:228-242, :298-315). The count is the number of screens (a handful), not anything that grows with the book, and it happens only when nothing is kept (first open, after Clear).
condition_or_scenario: A few extra small POSTs on a first open; no growth, no visible delay.
user_impact: none

title: Quotes are asked again with no check of how fresh the last one is
evidence: docs.rs:189-195 `opened` wakes the scheduler for any newly watched PRICED key (positions, exposure, markets, heatmap, cashflow, trade: due.rs:40); events.rs:187-201 calls it for each key a page newly watches; due.rs:128-131 `demand` + `read_quotes` then quote every held listing (due.rs:158-160) with no read of the stored quote's age; quotes.rs:110-170 asks the source for each; the stored `allowance` (cache.rs:222-235) is read by no gate.
condition_or_scenario: 1) The person, on the Trades tab, opens one trade page after another (each watches `trade:<id>`, App.svelte:200), or switches Dashboard -> Portfolio -> Markets. 2) Each newly watched priced key -> docs.rs:189-195 wake -> due.rs:104-131 pass. 3) Every held listing is quoted again from Yahoo/TMX/Cboe/Coinbase, though quoted seconds earlier. Ordinary: browsing trades and tabs.
user_impact: Every trade page or priced tab opened re-quotes every holding; nothing shown is wrong, but requests to the sources multiply with clicks (more chance a source refuses).

title: Background loops run with no page open
evidence: main.rs:237-252 spawns the loops at start. orders/readback.rs:477-498: with nothing open and nobody watching, `refresh_orders` still runs every ORDERS_IDLE_SEC=300 s (readback.rs:26) while signed in; feeds.rs:381-396 exposure loop runs `refresh_exposures` every 6 h; feeds.rs:3025-3056 archive loop re-reads bars when a stored read passes ARCHIVE_TOPUP_HOURS=20 (history.rs:693). None checks for an open page.
condition_or_scenario: 1) The app runs on the Pi (or desktop) with a saved Wealthsimple sign-in. 2) No browser has it open, e.g. overnight. 3) readback.rs:487-494 reads Wealthsimple's order feed every five minutes; the exposure and archive loops read sources on their timers. Ordinary: the app left running with no page.
user_impact: With no page open, Wealthsimple's order feed is still read every five minutes around the clock, and fund exposures and price bars are read on timers; nothing on screen is wrong.

title: The language model's file is hashed on every start, and its server is never stopped
evidence: main.rs:252 starts the disclosure reader at every start; feeds.rs:1541-1542 calls `summary_ensure` -> localmodel.rs:296-311 `ensure` -> `provision` (localmodel.rs:343-394), which, unless Ollama or BAGHOLDER_LLM_URL answers (localmodel.rs:188-201), calls `verified` twice (:365, :373), each a full SHA-256 read (localmodel.rs:396-413) of a 1,951,420,702-byte file (localmodel.rs:128-130). The model is on by default (decisions.md:22). `shutdown()` (localmodel.rs:517-532) has no caller; main.rs:280-287 stops without it.
condition_or_scenario: 1) The person starts Bagholder (or it restarts after an update). 2) The disclosure reader asks for the model; provision hashes the 1.95 GB llamafile twice before it starts the model server. 3) On exit, the model server is not stopped by the app; it survives wherever the exit does not signal the child (it is reused through its port on the next start, localmodel.rs:494-512). Ordinary: every start with the default model.
user_impact: After every start, about 3.9 GB is read and hashed before filing titles and summaries can be written (tens of seconds of disk on a Pi's SD card, not measured); the model process can outlive the app holding its memory.

title: Release binaries are not stripped and built without link-time optimisation
evidence: True: rust/Cargo.toml:21-23 `strip = false`, no lto or codegen-units. Effect is binary size and possibly a few percent of speed; no measurement shows a user-visible effect.
condition_or_scenario: Build configuration; nothing the person meets.
user_impact: none

title: Instants are stored as text that does not sort
evidence: True: book/src/text.rs:67-70 stores `t.to_string()`, fraction trimmed; orders.rs:213-214, :366/:371 and facts.rs:280 order or compare by that text. Text order differs from time order only when one instant's shorter fraction is a prefix of the other's digits, i.e. the two are within 10^-k s (k = the shorter fraction's length) or one is a whole second in the same second. The values come from the local clock (ns on Linux, us on macOS). The broker check, the one place it once mattered, moved to integer ns in 93a0dca3, whose message records no observed misorder.
condition_or_scenario: Needs two orders, brackets or declared reads stamped within ~10 ns-10 us of each other (or in the same second as a whole-second stamp); no evidence it has happened.
user_impact: Two orders or brackets stamped at almost the same instant could list in the wrong order.

title: Bars are fetched on a thread per symbol, with no bound
evidence: True: history.rs:991-1014 and :592-614 spawn one thread per symbol not already pending; each holds a cache connection from a pool that never waits (sqlite/src/pool.rs:11-13, history.rs:601-604) for the whole paced fetch. The burst is reachable: after Clear data with Market ticked (clear.rs:118-134, :157), the read-ahead (#425) asks every trade's chart and feeds.rs:3264-3271 starts a thread per instrument without bars (~200 here). The app raises no open-file limit (no setrlimit in rust/). No log, doc or commit records a failure from it.
condition_or_scenario: Harm needs the burst to exhaust a process limit (threads, or open files: each pooled cache connection holds several descriptors; macOS's default soft limit is 256); never observed.
user_impact: Usually nothing; at worst (not observed) ~200 simultaneous threads and cache connections could run the process out of files and make reads fail.

title: The broker pull commits one row at a time
evidence: broker/src/pull.rs:226-240 stores rows in a loop via store_row (:532); book/src/records.rs:120-126 `store` wraps each in `atomically` (book/src/lib.rs:123-131, BEGIN IMMEDIATE + commit); nothing encloses the pull (broker_reads.rs:395). Every commit syncs (sqlite/src/lib.rs:45 synchronous=FULL). The owner's book holds 14,606 broker records (docs/plans/stage-p-capacity-and-process.md:45). Incremental pulls read only what changed (decisions.md:85), so the cost is in a full pull.
condition_or_scenario: 1) The person connects Wealthsimple on a fresh install (e.g. the Pi), or runs Clear data with Wealthsimple's records ticked and syncs again. 2) The pull reads every account in full. 3) pull.rs:226-240 commits each of ~14,600 records separately, each with an fsync. Ordinary: a first sync or a re-sync after Clear.
user_impact: A full sync takes longer than a batched write would, by one disk sync per record (~14,600 here); the extra time is not measured.

title: Clear data leaves the cleared bytes in the files, is not one operation, and deletes every snapshot
evidence: Code facts true: no VACUUM/secure_delete (only `VACUUM INTO`, migrate.rs:264); clear.rs:145-177 runs steps one by one, refusing only while syncing; balances_now writes without the flag; clear.rs:164 removes all of snapshots/. But the update's rollback reads only snapshots taken since that update was put in place (update.rs:617-622, migrate.rs:271-273), so a Clear before an update leaves its rollback intact; free-page bytes are visible only to someone reading the raw file; a balances read (every 5 min while a page is open) must land inside the Clear's few seconds.
condition_or_scenario: Needs someone reading the raw database file, a Clear run during an update's trial window, or a balances read racing the Clear; no evidence of any.
user_impact: Cleared data would stay readable in the file's free pages to anyone inspecting it; a rare race could leave a row or lose a rollback snapshot.

title: The write-ahead log has no size limit
evidence: True: no journal_size_limit anywhere; passive checkpoint at 1,000 pages (sqlite/src/lib.rs:58, :93); TRUNCATE only for a replaced file (pool.rs:107). The -wal stays at its peak size until every connection closes (a restart). No doc, log or test records a large -wal on the owner's machines.
condition_or_scenario: Needs a write large enough that the -wal it leaves matters for disk space; never observed.
user_impact: The -wal file would stay as large as the largest write since start until the app restarts (disk space only).

title: Reading the book's id takes a write transaction
evidence: True: book/src/settings.rs:32-40 reads the id inside `atomically` (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, book/src/lib.rs:123-131); called from http/assets.rs:62 (every page load) and events.rs:300-301 (every stream connect). Writes are short transactions (import groups by percent, per-row pull commits); a failure returns '' and the page falls back to its last book (live.svelte.ts:178). No report of a slow page load.
condition_or_scenario: Needs a long-held write lock (e.g. a large Clear) at the moment the page loads or a stream connects; none observed.
user_impact: A page load would wait behind a long write.

title: The background filing reader has no bound
evidence: feeds.rs:1645-1647 `wants_reading` has no recency or count bound; feeds.rs:1659 stores up to 200 documents per listing; the sweep refreshes every held/watched listing when stale (feeds.rs:851-862) and opening a listing's Disclosures does too (feeds.rs:1841-1853); the reader (feeds.rs:1535-1569) reads every stored row wanting reading, newest first, until none remain; a row its source cannot name exactly is downloaded and read by the local model (feeds.rs:2053-2079), on by default (decisions.md:22).
condition_or_scenario: 1) The person holds or watches listings with regulatory filings (ordinary), or opens a listing's Disclosures. 2) refresh_filings stores up to 200 documents for each. 3) disclosure_read_loop downloads and model-reads every one of them, one after another every ~2 s plus the read, until the backlog is gone.
user_impact: After filings are stored, the app downloads and runs the local model over up to 200 documents per listing in the background until all are read, keeping the machine busy; nothing shown is wrong.

title: The Canada heatmap asks one paced request per constituent
evidence: universes.rs:283-311 `fetch_canada`: one constituents call then one `getQuoteBySymbol` per S&P/TSX 60 constituent, each after `pace("app-money.tmx.com", 0.6)`; a failed tile read is dropped by `.ok()` and the tile becomes `Not classified` (universes.rs:225), with no failure recorded. Read whenever a page shows the Canada heatmap and its rows are older than UNIVERSE_STALE_SEC=1800 (feeds.rs:2808-2818). Single failed requests do occur in the owner's use (decisions.md:34, 2026-10-02).
condition_or_scenario: 1) The person opens the heatmap on Canada with no rows stored, or keeps it shown past 30 minutes. 2) feeds.rs:2921 -> fetch_canada makes 61 requests at least 0.6 s apart: >= 36 s before the rows land. 3) If any one tile request fails, that constituent is filed under `Not classified` with no change, silently, until the next read.
user_impact: The Canada heatmap takes at least ~36 s to fill each read, and a tile whose request failed sits under 'Not classified' for half an hour with nothing saying why.

title: Requests have no total deadline, and retries and rests have no jitter
evidence: True: net/src/client.rs:141-169 per-operation timeouts only, no Instant/deadline in send_into (:655-789); sources/src/market.rs:86-92 pure doubling. A request hangs only if a source keeps the connection alive by dripping bytes slower than the read timeout; jitter matters for many clients retrying one server, not one person's app. No commit, doc or fixture records a stalled source.
condition_or_scenario: Needs a source to trickle a response indefinitely (never observed); the missing jitter has no single-user effect.
user_impact: A source that trickled bytes would hang that read and its loop indefinitely.

title: Rows the book could not place are not listed, and an import reports only counts
evidence: True: csv_import.rs:124 REPORT_NOTES=8; status.rs:297-366 header sentences only; no list of unplaced rows with raw fields (owner settled it, decisions.md:52). But commit 0b8ae381 (2026-10-03), which added the header sentence, states 'The owner's book has none.' The 9,030-problem example in SPEC.md:75 comes from a browser test fixture (web/e2e/menu.spec.ts:171). The per-file import report is SPEC trade-39's own definition.
condition_or_scenario: Needs Wealthsimple rows of a kind the mapping has no rule for, or a file naming an account the book does not hold; the owner's book had none as of 2026-10-03.
user_impact: Rows the book could not place would be counted in the header with no way to see which rows they are.

title: The order ticket silently rewrites what was typed
evidence: ticket/OrderTicket.svelte:58-70 `onBlur` drops the typed text and sets a quantity that is not > 0 to 1 (:65) and a bad price to null (:66-70); :78 `review()` does the same; :197 Review has no `disabled`; vals.ts:122-123 `parseNum` strips non-numeric characters, so empty or '0' -> 1. TradeDetail.svelte:150, :159 keep Buy on whatever the connection.
condition_or_scenario: 1) The person opens the ticket, clears the quantity to retype it (or types 0), then clicks elsewhere or presses Review. 2) OrderTicket.svelte:65 or :78 sets qty to 1 with no message; Review proceeds. Ordinary: editing a field.
user_impact: A cleared or zero quantity silently becomes 1 share (and a bad price silently empties); the person learns of it only on the review screen.

title: The trade list shows each trade's own currency but sorts and queues by CAD
evidence: views.rs:666 sorts the P&L column by `pnl_cad`; Trades.svelte:77 shows `money(t.pnl, t.currency)`; wire/build.rs:544 queues by `pnl_cad`. The owner trades in USD as well as CAD (US option contracts priced from Cboe's chains, decisions.md:90; USD-stated accounts, 8a11daed).
condition_or_scenario: 1) The book has a USD trade with P&L +100 (about +137 CAD) and a CAD trade with +120. 2) The person sorts Trades by P&L, descending. 3) views.rs:666 orders by CAD: the +100 USD row above the +120 CAD row. Ordinary: trades in two currencies.
user_impact: Sorted by P&L, the Trades list's P&L column as shown is out of order wherever trades in different currencies interleave.

title: The equity and monthly charts are not on a time axis, and the Value curve does not mark deposits
evidence: Dashboard.svelte:43-45 places points by index; engine/src/scope.rs:1117-1131 gives the P&L curve one point per day with a realized part; scope.rs:623-633 makes a month bar only where something was realized; wire/build.rs:507 points carry only date and value. Owner settled time spacing (decisions.md:52) and deposit marks (decisions.md:43), not built.
condition_or_scenario: 1) The book's sales are irregular in time (646 trades over three years). 2) The person opens the Dashboard's Equity card in P&L mode: days with sales are spaced evenly, so a quiet quarter takes the width of a busy week; the Monthly P&L skips months with no realized sale. 3) In Value mode no deposit or withdrawal is marked. Ordinary data.
user_impact: The P&L curve and monthly bars misstate time (gaps vanish, busy stretches stretch), and the Value curve shows no deposits or withdrawals.

title: An open trade's zero P&L is coloured as a gain, and the trade count disagrees with the P&L

title: The service recipes in the README do not restart a crash
evidence: README.md:109-114 launchd plist with RunAtLoad only, :133 schtasks with no restart (unchanged); the systemd recipe has Restart=on-failure and compose has restart: unless-stopped. The supervisor does not restart a crashed child outside an update window (update.rs:986 `return code`). The owner's Pi runs compose, which restarts (the 2.5.6 loop shows a restarter at work there). Nothing records the user running the launchd or schtasks recipe; decisions 2026-09-26: the app never sets itself up to start at login.
condition_or_scenario: Needs the user to run Bagholder on the Mac through the README's launchd recipe (or on Windows through schtasks) and the app to crash; neither is recorded.
user_impact: If it happened: after a crash the Mac copy stays down until the next login or a manual start.

title: The scheduler works out every fact the figures use after every change
evidence: True at f89634de: due.rs:101-142 `pass` runs on every wake; each record change wakes it (figures.rs:593-633 record_changed/pulled call wake()); it calls `e.needs()` (engine/src/needs.rs fact_needs: every transaction and every holding's unit history, in memory) and read_sources.rs:117-159 needs_of, which reads every transaction row from the book (`book.transactions()`, :124) and each payer's names (:155). At the owner's size (7,151 live transactions, 29 accounts, capacity.rs:58-73) this is a whole-book SQLite read per change, but on the scheduler thread, outside any request's answer (the added trade's answer is measured separately: 13.8 ms on the owner's copy, PR #507). No measurement of the pass exists.
condition_or_scenario: Trigger is ordinary (any added trade, note, pull). Missing to decide: the time of one due::pass after one change on the owner's copy or the capacity pair, on a Pi or scaled, and whether it delays anything the user waits on (quotes, the next read).
user_impact: Unknown; at worst some background CPU after each change, not a wait the user has been shown to meet.

title: Two stock dividends of one event share one Cashflow row id
evidence: Code fact true: engine/src/ledger.rs:1837 each StockDividend takes `transaction: anchor.clone()`; cashflow.rs:95-108 uses it as the row id. But no production input creates a stock-dividend leg (from == to with `cost`, ledger.rs:1820-1840): the only adjustment drafts are wealthsimple/src/mapping.rs:726 (split/consolidation/code change: units_per_unit and cost_share) and book/src/person.rs:226-247 (CostOfArrival has no `from` and returns early at ledger.rs:1811-1812, SpinOff, ReturnOfCapital). Found only by the generated property test (engine/tests/by_change.rs, PR #507 brief 27 item 3).
condition_or_scenario: Needs an event with two stock-dividend legs; no source mapping or entry form produces even one stock-dividend leg today, so no real data can reach it.
user_impact: If it happened: one of two stock-dividend rows in Cashflow could fail to update on screen.

title: A back-dated row matches its instrument's family from its first row, not from the row
evidence: True at f89634de: engine.rs:386-388 rematch_families matches each reached family whole (deep-history #514 not merged, so appended rows do the same). Measured (PR #507 body, CI run 38433354930): the depth pair, whose added trade targets a listing as deep as the owner's deepest (349 rows, capacity.rs:72), is within the 100 ms Pi budget at the owner's depth and misses it only at four times it (109.4 ms Pi); on a copy of the owner's book an added trade took 13.8 ms on the Mac. A back-dated row costs the same whole-family match as an appended one.
condition_or_scenario: Back-dated rows are ordinary (a Wealthsimple revision, a back-dated Add trade, a CSV of older history), but the excess is bounded by re-matching at most the owner's deepest family (349 rows), measured within budget at the owner's size; a slowdown needs a listing about four times deeper than any the owner has.
user_impact: None at the user's size; a back-dated change on a listing several times deeper than the owner's deepest could take a little over 100 ms on a Pi.

title: A coin remainder judged while its day's rate is pending stays open after the rate arrives
evidence: Code facts true: engine.rs:673-680 Change::Rates calls derive() and no rematch; dust.rs:38 converts the remainder's value at the row's day's rate. But fx.rs:103-105 `convert` returns at once when the currencies match, and every Wealthsimple coin is a CAD security (all crypto securities in the recorded replies: DOGE, DOT, ETH, FARTCOIN, FTM, SOL, USDC, currency CAD) priced at its CAD fill while the coin minimum is CAD (wealthsimple/src/mapping.rs:68-70); other brokers have no coin minimum (engine_inputs.rs:21-22), so nothing is dust. No rate is consulted, so none can be pending.
condition_or_scenario: Needs a coin whose currency differs from the broker's coin minimum's currency (a non-CAD coin at Wealthsimple) sold on a day whose Bank of Canada rate is not yet published; Wealthsimple has never sent such a coin.
user_impact: If it happened: a dust remainder would show as an open coin holding until some later change.
